index.name: Garbatrage Industrial Average
index.note: Proprietary. Not a benchmark. Not investment advice.
index.composition: Hand-picked mid-value securities, rebalanced when someone remembers

constituents.name: Trash & Sons
constituents.business: Third-generation residential collection. The sons are named Trash; the founder was not.
constituents.quote: We are a family business in the sense that nobody can leave.
constituents.lede: Third-generation residential collection across northwest Indiana. The sons are named Trash; the founder was not, and the family has declined to explain it for a hundred and eighteen years.

filings.text: Announces fourth son. No operational change disclosed; the filing is one page.
Collection rate expansion ahead of guidance for a second quarter. Fleet age disclosed, then discussed at length.
Board re-nominated without opposition. Succession proposal defeated for the ninth consecutive year.

constituents.name: Byte Bin
constituents.business: Certified e-waste destruction for enterprises that need the certificate more than the destruction.
constituents.filing: 10-Q — margin compression in the certificate line
constituents.quote: The hardware is the easy part. The paperwork is the moat.
constituents.lede: Certified e-waste destruction for enterprises that need the certificate more than the destruction, at a price that assumes you need the certificate very much indeed.

filings.text: Margin compression in the certificate line, which the company notes is more demanding than the destruction.
Expands certified-destruction capacity in a market where the certificate is widely believed to be the actual product.
Certification audit returned clean; the certificate certifying the certificate has been re-issued.

constituents.name: Morning Junk
constituents.business: Curbside bulk pickup sold as a subscription. Markets itself as a lifestyle brand to people with too much furniture.
constituents.quote: We are not a hauling company. We are a Saturday.
constituents.lede: Curbside bulk pickup sold as a subscription, marketed as a lifestyle brand to people with too much furniture and not enough Saturdays.

filings.text: Fourth attempt at going public. The prospectus is styled as a brand manifesto, which is filing the deck in a drawer as a design decision.
Subscription revenue concentrated in quarters ending in furniture acquisition, disclosed without a metric.
Announces a furniture-joy index as an unaudited exhibit. The index goes up when storage is full and is considered a trailing indicator.

constituents.name: Stable Value, Inc
constituents.business: Money-market administration. Has never had an exciting quarter and mentions this in every deck.
constituents.quote: We sell the absence of a story.
constituents.lede: Money-market administration that has never had an exciting quarter and confirms this in every deck, which is, it argues, the point.

filings.text: Board re-nominated unanimously, again. The meeting is not expected to be exciting, and is expected to say so.
Net asset value unchanged. Management highlights the absence of change as the product, with a chart.
Confirms the money-market portfolio is, as ever, a portfolio and a market, and that neither has done anything.

constituents.name: Hysterical Systems
constituents.business: Compactor and baler maintenance for retail chains. On-call, 24 hours, with a two-hour SLA nobody believes.
constituents.quote: Everyone is calm until the baler stops.
constituents.lede: Compactor and baler maintenance for retail chains, on call twenty-four hours, with a two-hour service-level agreement nobody has ever believed.

filings.text: CFO departs, citing the service-level agreement. The company reaffirms the SLA hours later, in full.
On-call revenue flat; on-call anger steady. Response-time incentives restructured around the two-hour promise.
Baler maintenance backlog reaches a record. The backlog itself is now the subject of a separate SLA.

constituents.name: Bin There Holdings
constituents.business: Roll-off container rental for construction. Name is a pun and the company is aware.
constituents.filing: 10-K — fleet age disclosed for the first time, stock falls
constituents.quote: We've been Bin There. It's on the trucks. It's not going anywhere.
constituents.lede: Roll-off container rental for construction. The name is a pun and the company is aware, and the trucks carry it everywhere.

filings.text: Fleet age disclosed for the first time; the stock falls. Management calls the disclosure 'honesty as a line item.'
Renames a container the 'Bin There Classic' while confirming there is nothing classic about it.
Construction starts down; container utilisation up. Net effect, management says, is 'still puns.'

constituents.name: Skip & Sons Hauling
constituents.business: Commercial roll-off and demolition debris. The sons are not involved and this is discussed at every shareholder meeting.
constituents.filing: DEF 14A — shareholder proposal on succession, defeated
constituents.quote: The sons have their own thing.
constituents.lede: Commercial roll-off and demolition debris. The sons are not involved, and this is discussed at every shareholder meeting.

filings.text: Shareholder proposal on succession defeated. The proposer noted the sons are not involved and were not running.
Demolition debris volume up on Seattle redevelopment; the company confirms none of the sons worked the sites.
Hires a logistics executive who is, the filing notes with some care, not a son.

constituents.name: Curbline Logistics
constituents.business: Route optimisation software sold to haulers, plus a small fleet used as a reference customer.
constituents.filing: 10-Q — reference fleet costs exceed software revenue
constituents.quote: We are our own worst client and our best case study.
constituents.lede: Route optimisation software sold to haulers, plus a small reference fleet kept largely to prove the software works on something with judgement.

filings.text: Reference fleet costs exceed software revenue for the third consecutive quarter. Management calls the fleet 'a lab,' then 'the point.'
Signs a hauling customer that is also, separately, on the reference-fleet list, creating what the company calls 'a closed loop.'
Discloses that route-optimisation revenue is optimised, but the routes, 'optimally, remain.'

constituents.name: Dumpster Dynamics
constituents.business: Manufactures the containers. Sells almost entirely to the same haulers who compete for the containers.
constituents.filing: 10-K — steel input costs, fourth consecutive warning
constituents.quote: Everyone needs a box. Nobody wants to buy one.
constituents.lede: Manufactures the containers many of its own customers compete to fill. Steel prices are discussed everywhere but the tariff disclosure.

filings.text: Steel input costs, fourth consecutive warning. The warning has become a section header in prior filings.
Container orders up as haulers hedge; the company hedges back by raising prices to the same haulers.
Announces a loyalty box program. The container comes out of the same steel, so loyalty is estimated, not measured.

constituents.name: Landfill Capital
constituents.business: Owns the holes. Leases airspace by the ton. Reports remaining capacity the way a mine reports reserves.
constituents.quote: We are a real estate company with a smell.
constituents.lede: Owns the holes. Leases airspace by the ton and reports remaining capacity the way a mine reports reserves, with the same chemistry of hope and paperwork.

filings.text: Airspace life extended to forty-one years. The extension is attributed to 'slower decomposition of the interest rate.'
Tonnage up; remaining capacity down, but slower. Management calls the margin 'inevitable but patient.'
Sells a capped cell to a competitor, then leases back the airspace, in a transaction the lawyers describe as 'complete.'

constituents.name: Scrapbook Materials
constituents.business: Ferrous and non-ferrous brokerage. The name has caused forty years of stationery jokes.
constituents.filing: 8-K — acquires a smaller broker with a normal name
constituents.quote: We bought them for the name. Partly.
constituents.lede: Ferrous and non-ferrous brokerage whose name has caused forty years of stationery jokes, and which keeps the name precisely because of them.

filings.text: Acquires a smaller broker with a normal name. The company confirms the normal name was a consideration.
Ferrous margins steady; stationery joke volume steady. Both are trended in the exhibit.
Official company color changed to a metallics; the palette is described as 'also a material.'

constituents.name: Pulp & Patience
constituents.business: Recovered fibre. The patience refers to the permitting.
constituents.quote: Nothing in this business is fast except the pulp.
constituents.lede: Recovered fibre mill in Bangor. The patience in the name is the permitting, which has been the business for ninety-five years.

filings.text: Mill restarts after fourteen months idle. The permitting that caused the idle is described as 'still a work of art.'
Recovered-fibre prices weak; recovery rates strong; patience, the company notes, is constant.
Applies for a permit to upgrade the permit office, which is awaiting a permit.

constituents.name: Rota Composting
constituents.business: Municipal organics processing. Odour complaints are the primary KPI and are reported quarterly.
constituents.quote: Our best quarter was a quiet one.
constituents.lede: Municipal organics processing in Portland, where odour complaints are the primary KPI and are reported quarterly, usually with relief.

filings.text: Complaint volume down twelve percent, stock up nine percent. Management calls the correlation 'a quiet one.'
Organic intake up. Odour remediation capex up. KPI commentary is, for once, positive and aspirational.
Open house scheduled at the newest pile; parking is perpendicular, which management notes is itself progress.

constituents.name: Odor Neutral
constituents.business: Enzyme treatment for transfer stations. Sells to exactly the operators who generate the complaints.
constituents.filing: 10-Q — customer concentration, top three are 61% of revenue
constituents.quote: We are a hedge against Rota's KPI.
constituents.lede: Enzyme treatment for transfer stations, selling deodorisation to exactly the operators whose KPIs are measured in complaints.

filings.text: Customer concentration — top three are sixty-one percent of revenue. The top three are the operators who generate the complaints.
Enzyme efficiency improved. The KPI of the customers improved, which the company describes as a compliment.
Discloses that its best quarter was Rota's best quarter, and that correlation is, for once, the strategy.

constituents.name: Gull Trust
constituents.business: Royalty trust holding a share of landfill gas rights. Pays monthly, explains nothing.
constituents.quote: The trust does not give guidance. The trust distributes.
constituents.lede: Royalty trust holding a share of landfill gas rights. Pays monthly, explains nothing, and declines to give guidance on principle.

filings.text: Distribution maintained at prior level. The one-line press release is considered a model of the genre.
Landfill gas rights stable; distribution declared and paid, with the schedule attached and nothing else.
Explains, in a rare break from practice, that it will not be explaining anything, and declines to amend.

constituents.name: Pigeon Property Group
constituents.business: Buys brownfield sites, remediates partially, leases to storage and logistics.
constituents.quote: Partially remediated is a business model, not an apology.
constituents.lede: Buys brownfield sites, remediates them partially, and leases the result to storage and logistics, treating partial as a feature.

filings.text: Remediation overruns at three sites. The company amends the word 'partial' in its description to 'partially more.'
Storage and logistics occupancy up on brownfield demand; the remedial shortfall is disclosed in the same paragraph.
Declares partial remediation a business model 'rather than an apology,' and files it as such.

constituents.name: Raccoon Brands
constituents.business: Household storage and bins, sold DTC, named after animals that get into bins.
constituents.quote: The animal is aspirational. The customer wants to keep things out.
constituents.lede: Household storage and bins sold direct-to-consumer, named after animals that get into bins, on the theory that the customer knows the animal.

filings.text: Customer acquisition cost disclosed for the first time; investors recalibrate. The bin itself is unchanged.
Direct-to-consumer storage revenue up ahead of a hoarding season analysts had not calendared.
Contest to name a new bin results in 'Raccoon's Revenge'; the company accepts it on the record.

constituents.name: Sludge Works
constituents.business: Biosolids handling for municipal water districts. Contracts run decades and are won on patience.
constituents.quote: Nobody celebrates us and nobody replaces us.
constituents.lede: Biosolids handling for municipal water districts, where contracts run decades and are won on patience and a quiet temperament.

filings.text: Three contracts renewed, all twenty-year. The tenure, management notes, is both the point and the entire presentation.
Biosolids volumes steady; municipal budgets steady; the patience on both is disclosed as operational.
Confirms it is replacing nobody and being replaced by nobody, in a filing of unusual confidence.

constituents.name: Tangible Waste
constituents.business: Waste audits for ESG reporting. Produces the number, then sells the reduction against the number.
constituents.filing: 10-Q — audit revenue and reduction revenue diverge
constituents.quote: We find the problem and then we are the solution. Sequentially.
constituents.lede: Waste audits for ESG reporting. Produces the number, then sells the reduction against the number, sequentially and in that order.

filings.text: Audit revenue and reduction revenue diverge. The company calls the gap, plainly, the business.
Reduction sold against its own audit is disclosed as a method, then as 'sequentially.'
Produces a corporate average that is later disclosed to be the number, which was the point.

constituents.name: Brownfield Partners
constituents.business: Industrial redevelopment. Buys what nobody will touch and touches it.
constituents.quote: Every asset we own was somebody's problem first.
constituents.lede: Industrial redevelopment in Cleveland that buys what nobody will touch and touches it, usually with a union and a deadline.

filings.text: Portfolio occupancy ninety-four percent. The company notes the remaining six percent were deliberately somebody's problem.
Redevelopment starts up; the cleared parcels are described as 'ready to be somebody's problem again.'
Acquires a site no one else bid on, calling it 'the honest price' and the rest of the market 'polite.'

constituents.name: Leaf & Leave
constituents.business: Seasonal yard-waste subscription. Revenue is 71% in a nine-week window and the company is at peace with it.
constituents.filing: 10-Q — Q2 concentration disclosed as a risk
constituents.quote: We are a nine-week company and the other 43 are for planning.
constituents.lede: Seasonal yard-waste subscription whose revenue is seventy-one percent in a nine-week window, a fact the company is at peace with.

filings.text: Second-quarter concentration disclosed as a risk, then as the business, then as 'the point of the year.'
Nine-week revenue window confirmed; the other forty-three weeks are described as for planning the window.
Winter subscriber churn disclosed as 'seasonal,' which is confirmed to mean the subscribers return in spring with leaves.

constituents.name: Mossback Industrial
constituents.business: Heavy equipment refurbishment. Buys back its own machines at 12 years and resells at 15.
constituents.quote: A machine is not old. It is between owners.
constituents.lede: Heavy-equipment refurbishment that buys back its own machines at twelve years and resells them at fifteen, between owners.

filings.text: Refurbishment mix now thirty-eight percent of revenue. The machines, management notes, are between owners.
Buys back its own machines at twelve years; resells at fifteen. The three years are called the value-add.
Opens a fourth refurbishment bay, sized deliberately for the machines it already sold twice.

constituents.name: Gravel & Grit
constituents.business: Aggregate supply for road base. Owns three pits, permits two, operates one.
constituents.filing: 8-K — second pit permitted after six years
constituents.quote: The permits are the business. The gravel is the byproduct.
constituents.lede: Aggregate supply for road base in Wichita. Owns three pits, has permits for two, and actively operates one, in that declining order.

filings.text: Second pit permitted after six years of review. The gravel underneath is described as having aged.
Reports operating one of three owned pits, holding permits for two, and 'discussing' the third.
Aggregate demand up; available aggregate flat; the differential is disclosed as the thesis.

constituents.name: Sort-Right Systems
constituents.business: Optical sorting retrofits for MRFs. Sells throughput; accuracy is the customer's problem to staff.
constituents.quote: The machine is right. The line is only as good as the people beside it.
constituents.lede: Optical sorting retrofits for material-recovery facilities, selling throughput while leaving staffing of the line, and the accuracy, to the customer.

filings.text: Backlog up, installs slip. The company calls the divergence 'a quality we are improving at.'
Throughput sold as throughput, accuracy excluded. The line, the company notes, is staffed by the customer.
Optical sort retrofits pass a certification that was written, helpfully, by a retrofit vendor.

constituents.name: Reclaim Collective
constituents.business: Worker-owned co-op doing commercial recycling. Same CEO as STBL, which nobody has noticed.
constituents.quote: We are a co-op. Decisions take a month and last a decade.
constituents.lede: Worker-owned commercial-recycling co-op in Detroit whose membership takes a month to decide anything and a decade to make it stick.

filings.text: Membership buyout tranche funded. The decision to fund it took a month; the cheque cleared in a decade.
Co-op commercial volumes steady. Management declines to call it steady growth, citing the constitution.
Announces a vote on a new paint color for the bins. The bins observe, pending the consensus of the committee.
